title: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors: full refresh of a custom connector's data source through Microsoft Graph
summary: Hold: the briefing assumes that existing connection permissions and allowed application IDs authorize the planned full sync, although Microsoft has not documented its authorization requirements. It also overstates how long deleted items remain searchable and understates the documented admin-centre operations for partner connections.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft plans a Graph API full refresh of custom connectors' existing data sources for administrators and developers.
claims.quote: Admins and developers can do a full refresh or sync of their datasource for Custom Connectors using Graph APIs.

claims.quote: This also ensures that any items deleted in the source are automatically deleted during this full sync

claims.claim: The planned full sync removes the need for separate delete APIs for source deletions.
claims.quote: admins do not have to use separate delete APIs to do this.

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors were formerly called Microsoft Graph connectors.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 Copilot connectors (formerly Microsoft Graph connectors)

claims.claim: The Copilot connector APIs are a way to build a custom synced connector.
claims.quote: You can create a synced Copilot connector in one of three ways: ... Use the Copilot connector APIs
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/plugins/overview-copilot-connector to sources; it supports the cited connectors-overview statements.

claims.claim: Each indexed source item is represented as an externalItem with a unique item ID.
claims.quote: Each item from your data source must be represented as an externalItem in Microsoft Graph with a unique item ID.

claims.claim: The item guide documents adding an individual item by assigning its identifier in the URL.
claims.quote: To add an item to the index, you create an externalItem. When you create an item, you assign a unique identifier in the URL.

claims.claim: The item guide documents updating an individual item using its unique identifier.
claims.quote: you can update its entry in the index by updating the externalItem, using the unique identifier assigned to the item when you created it.

claims.where: controls[1].api; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: DELETE /v1.0/external/connections/{connectionsId}/items/{externalItemId} removes one indexed external item.
claims.quote: Delete an externalItem object. DELETE /external/connections/{connectionsId}/items/{externalItemId} ... DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr/items/TSP228082938

claims.claim: The item guide describes a full crawl as capturing all additions and deletions.
claims.quote: Full crawl: Updates the entire item from the source data (re-crawl), capturing all additions and deletions

claims.claim: The item guide leaves the choice of refresh strategy to the connector owner.
claims.quote: Ultimately, the choice of data refresh strategy depends on your data type and computing capabilities.

claims.claim: The SDK connector agent already detects source deletions during periodic full crawls and deletes those items from the index.
claims.quote: The agent is capable of detecting items deleted from your data source based on the items sent by your connector during periodic full crawls. The agent then takes care of deleting the item from the Microsoft index as well.

claims.where: controls[0]; What's changing; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet document the roadmap's custom Graph full-sync operation or an admin-centre setting for that operation.
claims.quote: Searched: custom connectors full refresh full sync Graph API admin switch; externalConnection full sync configuration. Opened externalConnection beta/v1.0, API overview, manage-connector and SDK overview; SDK crawls are separate, not the planned Graph operation.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The arrival default of the new full-sync capability is not stated, and no source says existing connections change automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot custom connectors full refresh full sync default admin switch. Read roadmap ('can do'), externalConnection beta/v1.0, API overview and manage-connector; none states the planned full-sync arrival default.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described the new Graph full sync's deletion-detection or interrupted-run semantics.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph externalConnection full sync refresh start complete synchronization custom connector permission; externalConnection full sync configuration. Opened beta/v1.0 resource and item guide; SDK detection is documented, but the planned Graph operation is not.

claims.claim: The permission required by the planned full-sync operation is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Graph externalConnection full sync refresh start complete synchronization custom connector permission. Opened externalConnection beta/v1.0 and delete/update references; existing permissions are documented, but no full-sync permission is stated.

claims.claim: ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is the least privileged delete permission and ExternalItem.ReadWrite.All is the higher permission.
claims.quote: Application | ExternalItem.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalItem.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: Microsoft does not document deleting an individual indexed custom-connector item through the admin UI or index browser.
claims.quote: Searched: custom connector delete index browser; Copilot custom connector delete individual indexed item UI. Opened manage-connector and indexed-content; they describe connection deletion and item inspection, not individual item deletion.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/external/connections/{connectionsId} can update the connection's configuration property.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated. ... configuration ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections/contosohr

claims.claim: ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy is the least privileged permission for updating a connection.
claims.quote: Application | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.OwnedBy | ExternalConnection.ReadWrite.All

claims.claim: An admin-centre UI for configuring a connection's additional allowed application IDs is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot connectors additional application admin center; custom connector configuration allowed apps UI. Opened manage-connector, connectors overview and Graph update reference; configuration is documented as a Graph property, not a portal control.

claims.claim: The configuration property specifies additional application IDs allowed to manage a connection and index content into it.
claims.quote: Specifies additional application IDs that are allowed to manage the connection and to index content in the connection.

claims.claim: Every app listed in configuration could run the planned full sync once that operation exists.
claims.quote: Searched: externalConnection full sync configuration; Graph externalConnection full sync refresh synchronization custom connector permission. Read update reference and beta/v1.0 resource; no passage authorizes those apps for the unpublished operation.
claims.fix: Remove '; each one is an app that could run a full sync on that connection once the operation exists'. Retain the documented description of configuration.

claims.claim: The connectors FAQ says incremental crawls do not handle deletions and removed source items remain indexed.
claims.quote: Doesn't handle deletions, so items removed from the data source remain in the index.

claims.claim: Items deleted at source stay searchable today until the connector deletes them.
claims.quote: If connection failures prevent delete detection from running reliably, items that aren't rediscovered during crawls for 28 days are automatically removed from the Microsoft 365 index to maintain compliance.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'For API-built custom connectors, Microsoft's item guide documents removal by deleting the externalItem using its unique identifier; the roadmap plans automatic source-deletion cleanup during the new full sync.' See https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/connecting-external-content-manage-items.

claims.claim: Indexed connector content can surface in Microsoft Search and Copilot answers.
claims.quote: Synced and federated connectors power Microsoft 365 Copilot and other Microsoft 365 intelligent experiences, such as Microsoft Search ... Users can find, summarize, and learn from this content using natural language prompts.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The admin centre's supported operations for partner and custom-built connections are connection deletion and name and description editing only.
claims.quote: Admins can control the visibility of partner connectors in Copilot and Copilot Search via a simple toggle.
claims.fix: Replace the operations statements with: 'For partner connections, the supported-operations table lists connection deletion and name and description editing.' This limits the statement to the table rather than implying that the page documents no other operations.
